question: How do intermolecular interactions between pharmaceutical compounds affect their binding behavior on mineral surfaces like goethite?
answer: Intermolecular interactions between pharmaceutical compounds significantly influence their binding behavior on goethite surfaces. Kinetic and equilibrium adsorption experiments revealed that nalidixic acid (NA) enhances the adsorption of niflumic acid (NFA) through cobinding interactions, while no such effect occurs with sulfamethoxazole (SMX). The adsorption was pH-dependent, with optimal binding observed at pH 6, and desorption tests confirmed high recovery rates (99 ± 2%). High-performance liquid chromatography analysis confirmed distinct retention times for each compound, enabling precise quantification. These findings demonstrate that drug-drug interactions can either promote or have no effect on mineral surface binding, depending on molecular compatibility.

The findings highlight the importance of understanding drug cobinding mechanisms for predicting the environmental fate of pharmaceutical mixtures.
